best_for: People who want an encrypted messenger that does not ask for a phone number or email, and who accept fewer features in return.
description:
Session is an end-to-end encrypted messenger that is built as a decentralized app. The desktop app is open source under GPL-3.0 and published by Oxen Labs. The Session Technology Foundation, a Swiss foundation, backs the wider Session ecosystem and gives grants to people who work on it.

You can turn on disappearing messages, keep your own encryption keys under your control, and give the app a custom theme. The code is public, so anyone can read and audit it. If you want to know how it works before you trust it, the site has a whitepaper and a shorter litepaper on the protocol, and the foundation publishes transparency reports.

points.title: No phone number
points.text: You sign up with a generated Account ID, not a phone number or email. A recovery password, a list of words in a set order, restores that ID on another device.

points.title: Routed through a node network
points.text: Messages travel over an onion-routed network run by community nodes, so no single server sees both sender and receiver. Session says it collects no location or device metadata.

points.title: Limits to know
points.text: Attachments top out at 10 MB and groups at 100 people; larger groups use Communities. Restoring an account brings back only the last 14 days of messages.

points.title: Calls are a beta
points.text: Voice and video calls are off by default and one-to-one only. Calls are direct, so your IP address is visible to the other person and to a relay server.

points.title: Desktop extras
points.text: The desktop app can lock its local database with a PIN or password and strips EXIF data from files you send, except videos.

points.title: Free, with a Pro tier
points.text: The project says Session will always be free to use. A paid Session Pro exists to fund the network; its features and price were not listed on the pages read.

points.title: Builds and versions
points.text: The Flathub Flatpak is verified and x64 only. Windows installs per user or for all users; Macs need macOS 13 with Intel and Apple silicon builds. Windows keeps 65 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
